# Raquel Miranda

Instructional Designer · LLM Evaluator · Educational Technologist

Website: https://raquel-miranda.netlify.app

## About

I'm a psychopedagogue and instructional designer based in Brazil. Nearly a decade evaluating large language models for platforms like Leapforce, Appen, and Teamwork gave me technical intuition that most designers don't have, before AI evaluation became an industry unto itself.

My foundation is in psychopedagogy and epistemology. What that means in practice: I ask what it means to know something before I decide how to teach it. I build tools that treat learners as thinking agents.

The theory comes first. The design follows.

Skills: Instructional Design, LLM Evaluation, Cognitive Science, E-Learning, Epistemology, AI & Education, LXD, Python, Vanilla JS, Claude API, n8n, Figma, Prompt Engineering, ADDIE, UDL, NVC

## Projects

### Conflict Resolution Simulator
URL: https://conflictsim.com
Case study: https://raquel-miranda.netlify.app/case-study.pdf
Type: Interactive Training · AI-Powered
Stack: Vanilla JS · Claude API
Year: 2025–26

A role-play simulator for navigating four distinct workplace conflict archetypes. Characters respond to how you communicate — empathy opens them up, blame closes them down. Powered by character-specific AI prompts with consistent psychological profiles. Built in Vanilla JS by design: no framework, no dependencies, no build step.

Four scenarios: Lucas (missed deadline), Rita (idea theft), Daniel (scope creep), Marina (angry client). Each runs in Normal and Challenge mode. After each session, a second AI model analyzes the conversation and delivers structured feedback across four skill dimensions with a radar chart.

### Selly — AI Sales Coach
URL: https://b2b-sales-trainer.netlify.app
Case study: https://raquel-miranda.netlify.app/selly-case-study.pdf
Type: AI Coach · B2B Sales Training
Stack: Vanilla JS · Claude API · Netlify Functions
Year: 2025–26

A conversational coach for B2B sales reps. Users pick their struggle areas, choose how much scaffolding they want, and Selly runs the session from there — pushing back when answers are vague, quoting the rep's own words in feedback because abstract feedback is easy to ignore.

The design started with a 34-page knowledge base built before writing a line of the system prompt. Five topic areas: Objection Handling, Discovery, Reading the Buyer, Timing and Qualification, Value Selling. Two modes: Coach (minimal scaffolding) and Guide (more structure). The complexity in this project was instructional.
